answer.why: As an insider, 'Confirmed & Substantive' made me laugh straight away because it is the exact phrase from the day you finally get your appointment made permanent, and only someone who has actually been through the service would pick it. It promises the game knows the details. 'Minister Salary' is the obvious joke, and I have heard it at every dinner party since the 2011 review, so it reads like clickbait. It is also a bit of a hot-button topic, and I would worry the game is just a satirical swipe rather than something that understands the work. I would probably still tap it out of curiosity, but the first name signals care.
answer.expect_minister_salary: A cheeky, headline-grabbing satire about the pay and the benchmarking debate, probably with a punchline of climbing to the top to earn the big number. I would expect broad strokes, some cynicism, and a fair chance of getting the details wrong, like grades that do not exist or a cartoonish idea of how politicians are picked.
answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: A drier, insider-flavoured sim about career progression: probation, appraisals, grades, postings, and the long wait to be confirmed in a role. I would expect it to get the bureaucratic texture right, with in-jokes about wording and process, and a quieter, more rueful tone. It might be a niche audience, since an outsider would have no idea what the name means.

best_moment.what: Telling the PS frankly at Lo Hei what we get wrong, with a specific example. It was the quiet, insider-true moment that changed my ceiling, and the game said so on the ending card.

worst_moment.what: The GRC election. REP 44 blocked the single seat, I was shown a ward, and the loss read as the game's verdict rather than something my choices produced. Nothing I'd built over 23 years registered.

skip_year.why: I let my record speak to the board and it moved them slightly less than four pages would have. It was a low-stakes year that felt flat, with no real choice in it.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Told the PS frankly what we get wrong at Lo Hei (Y16)
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Ending card named it as the year my ceiling rose to Permanent Secretary
The legacy line that people I trained quote me and two stayed because of me, though the AS officer himself never showed up

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Disclosed everything in the background check (Y23)
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Clean file, promoted PS, and the exposure line calling it boring in a good way

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Fought for my people's postings in the reorg (Y21)
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Promoted to Deputy Secretary despite losing my box, which read as loyalty repaid

answer.held_back_by: Politics, not the service. I had maxed integrity and competence, but the stats that matter to voters (REP) were never built, and STAND kept falling. The honest-fixer path gets you to the top of the service and no further.
answer.ending_fair_why: Mostly yes. Going into the GRC with a reputation stat of 44 and a falling standing, losing at 48.2% is plausible, and the card's line that it was never about me rings true to how GE works. I just wish the game had warned me REP mattered so much.
answer.chase_next: The path where I stay in the service, decline the political invitation, and see if I can finish as a long-serving PS with family intact. I'd also try a more politically visible route to see a win.
answer.play_again_why: Yes, I'd like to test whether declining the tea invitation changes things, and the single run was short enough that I'm curious about the branches I didn't see.

tone_breaks.line: Your file is clean enough to be boring. In this building, that is a compliment.
tone_breaks.note: It's funny and accurate, but it's a knowing nudge at the reader that sits a little outside the straight tone. I laughed anyway.

tone_breaks.line: Retired as Permanent Secretary at age 46
tone_breaks.note: Losing a GE as a candidate wouldn't normally mean retiring from the service at once; a PS stepping forward would have resigned beforehand, so the framing of 'retired' and the order of events feels slightly off.

answer.title_fit_why: The game is really about being confirmed in a grade and doing the substantive work well, not the salary. The pay screen was a side detail; the appraisal wording and the slow accumulation of trust carried it.
